title: debug-sink-replaces-silent-device
intention: BaseDevice gets a debug_sink property (defaults to self) that every device's logging calls route through. The silent_device sieve checks for self.debug_sink.emit() call sites instead of self.emit(). Each device declares its own sink: most use the default (self), inference_domain overrides with its trail. The module-level _trail.emit() calls in inference_domain/domain.py are replaced by self.debug_sink.emit() routed through the device instance. Harbor_master and charter get their actual emit calls added at the same time, going through the default self sink.
why: Three devices fail the silent_device sieve (harbor_master, inference_domain, charter). inference_domain already logs through _trail.emit() — a module-level singleton that predates the BaseDevice pattern — but the sieve can't see it because it checks self.emit(). Teaching the sieve about _trail specifically (option 2) works today but requires a new sieve touch for every future logging shape. The debug_sink contract means each device declares its path once and the sieve never needs to learn device-specific internals again. Akien: 'that does bring it into alignment with my head.'
traces_to: Law 4 — the debug_sink is the physics that replaces the silent_device sieve's AST-pattern-matching policy
Law 7 — errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces; a device that inherits emit() and never fires it is silent at every crossing
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a BaseDevice subclass can be instantiated without debug_sink being set; (2) inference_domain's logging still goes through the module-level _trail instead of through self.debug_sink; (3) the silent_device sieve still scans for self.emit() instead of self.debug_sink.emit(); (4) harbor_master or charter remain without emit calls after the build. WRONG INTENT if: debug_sink becomes a feature flag for turning logging off — the sink is WHERE it goes, not WHETHER it fires.
constraints: inference_domain's resolve() currently takes no device reference — threading debug_sink requires passing the sink (or the device) into the module-level functions
the _trail singleton holds state (held_diagnostics, diagnostic_trail) beyond just emit — only the emit path moves to debug_sink, the rest stays
how: 1. Add self.debug_sink = self to BaseDevice.__init__. 2. Update silent_device sieve to check self.debug_sink.emit() call sites. 3. InferenceDomainDevice overrides debug_sink with its trail object. 4. Thread the sink from the device instance into domain.py's resolve() so _trail.emit() calls become sink.emit() calls. 5. Add self.debug_sink.emit() calls to harbor_master and charter at their meaningful state transitions. 6. Re-seal affected proofs.
watchme: none, because debug_sink adds logging plumbing — correctness is proved by the sieve going green, not by runtime observation
